Q: How do you keep evaluation semantics stable when changing libraries or dashboards?
A: A library provides collection, execution and reporting mechanisms; your evaluation contract defines dataset identity, metric meaning, aggregation and failure policy. Export raw per-case outcomes and version configuration so a dashboard change does not silently change acceptance. Check how missing results, judge errors, retries and skipped cases enter the denominator. Run a small shared fixture through both implementations before comparing their totals. Provider integration convenience does not establish that two similarly named metrics measure the same quantity.
Why: One runner excludes timed-out cases and another counts them as failures. Their reported success rates cannot be compared directly even if both dashboards call the metric 'pass rate'.
Risk: A changed denominator can look like a quality improvement.
Trade: Separate portable metric definitions from provider-specific collection adapters.
Try: Reconcile per-case results and denominators across two evaluation reports.
